guard_patterns.handling: Require directly accessible official public source.
Preserve publication edition and reference period.
Keep activity, installations, energy, capacity, forecasts and emissions distinct.
Keep modelled, estimated, forecast, reported and measured values distinct.
Preserve UK, GB, England, sector, scheme, airport, site and accounting boundaries.
Retain provisional, forecast, correction and revision status.
Preserve CO2, CO2e, energy, capacity, count, tonnage, rate and accounting scope.
Retain uncertainty, survey, model, coverage, lag and scheme limitations.
No parcel value without parcel identity, geometry, compatible activity and method binding.
Every package must pass deterministic structure and scope checks.

packages.title: ONS renewable/waste source-scope QA
facts: ONS Environmental Accounts publishes UK energy use from renewable and waste sources by source and industry.
The current dataset covers 1990 to 2024.
Renewable and waste energy sources include categories such as wind, hydro and solar.
The dataset is an energy-use dataset, not a cadastral emissions measurement dataset.
Industry breakdowns use SIC-based categories rather than parcel boundaries.
ONS states that statistics may be revised when further data become available.
ONS also states that revisions can result from method or system changes.
Planned revisions are distinguished from corrections of genuine errors.
Energy use from renewable sources is not identical to renewable electricity generation.
No parcel value can be inferred from the national or industry series without parcel-specific activity evidence.

packages.title: ONS renewable-heat technology-scope QA
facts: ONS publishes energy use from renewable sources used to generate heat.
The series covers 1990 to 2024.
The published scope includes active solar heating.
The published scope includes heat pumps.
The published scope includes geothermal aquifers.
The dataset measures energy use rather than direct parcel greenhouse gas emissions.
A technology category does not establish the location of an individual installation.
A national energy-use total cannot be treated as a meter reading.
Revision status must be preserved when comparing editions.
Parcel attribution requires a separate identity, geometry and activity-data gate.

packages.title: ONS residence/territorial bridge QA
facts: UK Environmental Accounts greenhouse gas estimates use a residence basis.
The residence basis includes emissions from UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever they occur.
Territorial greenhouse gas statistics use a different geographic accounting boundary.
ONS publishes bridging tables between Environmental Accounts measures and UNFCCC-style measures.
Residence-basis and territorial totals must not be substituted for one another.
Industry attribution on the residence basis is not a cadastral parcel attribution.
International transport treatment can differ between accounting bases.
Comparisons require the accounting basis to be retained explicitly.
Any conversion between bases is a statistical bridge rather than a parcel observation.
Parcel-level emissions remain unsupported without compatible parcel-specific evidence.

packages.title: ONS direct-energy renewable-share QA
facts: ONS estimated UK direct energy use at 165.4 Mtoe in 2024.
ONS reported fossil fuels as 77.7% of direct energy use in 2024.
ONS reported renewable sources as 15.3% of direct energy use in 2024.
Natural gas was the largest single fossil-fuel source in the ONS summary.
Wind, wave and tidal formed the largest renewable source grouping in the ONS summary.
Direct energy use is an economy-wide statistic.
A renewable share is not the same measure as electricity-generation share.
Energy-share statistics are not direct greenhouse gas measurements.
National shares cannot be assigned to an individual parcel by default.
Any parcel calculation would require parcel-specific fuel or electricity activity data.

packages.title: DESNZ Q1-2026 MPP-versus-all-generators QA
facts: DESNZ Energy Trends reported January to March 2026 energy statistics on 28 May 2026.
Major Power Producer electricity generation rose by 1.6% versus the same period a year earlier.
Major Power Producer renewable generation rose by 23% in that comparison.
Major Power Producer gas generation fell by 17% in that comparison.
Renewables provided 51.7% of Major Power Producer generation in the reported period.
Gas provided 35.1% of Major Power Producer generation in the reported period.
Nuclear provided 12.4% of Major Power Producer generation in the reported period.
Major Power Producer statistics are not automatically equivalent to all-generator quarterly statistics.
Generation mix is not a parcel electricity-consumption measurement.
Any downstream emissions use must preserve the generator-population and reporting-period scope.

packages.title: DESNZ temperature-adjusted energy QA
facts: DESNZ reported primary energy consumption on both unadjusted and temperature-adjusted bases.
For January to March 2026, unadjusted primary energy consumption fell by 3.0% year on year.
For the same period, temperature-adjusted consumption fell by 1.5%.
Temperature adjustment changes interpretation of energy-demand trends.
Adjusted and unadjusted series must not be mixed silently.
Primary energy consumption differs from final electricity consumption.
Energy consumption changes do not directly state greenhouse gas changes.
Quarterly national trends are not parcel observations.
The comparison period must be retained when reporting percentage changes.
Parcel estimates require local activity evidence rather than national temperature-adjusted averages.

packages.title: DESNZ renewable capacity-versus-generation QA
facts: DESNZ renewable statistics cover both installed capacity and electricity generation.
Installed capacity and generated electricity are distinct measures.
Energy Trends includes quarterly renewable electricity capacity and generation tables.
Renewable statistics also cover heat generation and transport fuels in separate series.
Capacity does not establish actual output during a specific hour or day.
Generation does not identify the consuming parcel.
Load factors are a separate concept from installed capacity.
Certificate-based scheme data may have reporting lags.
Technology and reporting-period fields must be preserved in comparisons.
No parcel emissions value should be inferred from national renewable capacity alone.

packages.title: Renewables Obligation certificates-versus-generation QA
facts: DESNZ publishes monthly Renewables Obligation certificate and generation information.
The series relates to certificates issued for qualifying generation under the Renewables Obligation.
Certificates are an administrative scheme measure.
A certificate count is not itself an electricity-meter reading at a consuming site.
Certificate issuance and physical generation timing can differ.
RO data should not be treated as the complete UK electricity-generation inventory.
The scheme boundary must be retained when using certificate statistics.
Administrative scheme data do not identify cadastral parcels consuming the electricity.
Any emissions calculation must use a compatible physical activity basis.
Parcel attribution remains a separate gate.

packages.title: Renewables Obligation reporting-lag QA
facts: DESNZ notes that some Renewables Obligation certificate and generation data are three months in arrears.
The publication page is updated monthly for the relevant scheme tables.
A publication date is not necessarily the same as the generation reference period.
Current-page status must therefore be separated from reference-period status.
Late administrative updates can change recent scheme totals.
Reporting lag must be retained in freshness scoring.
A lagged certificate series should not be presented as real-time electricity generation.
Scheme lag does not imply missing national generation data from all other sources.
Parcel-specific activity cannot be backfilled from scheme lagged aggregates.
QA must preserve both publication date and underlying reference period.

packages.title: DfT aviation forecast model-versus-observation QA
facts: DfT published the UK aviation forecast 2026 on 18 June 2026.
The publication contains forecasts for air passengers.
It contains forecasts for aircraft movements.
It contains forecasts for CO2 emissions for UK airports.
The forecasts are a long-term strategic modelling product.
The 2026 forecasts update the forecast set published in 2017.
Forecast outputs are not observations of realised future traffic or emissions.
Model assumptions and scenario definitions must accompany any forecast value.
Airport-level forecast data are not cadastral parcel emissions measurements.
Forecast values must never be substituted for measured parcel emissions.

packages.title: DfT aviation CO2-versus-GHG scope QA
facts: The DfT aviation forecast publication explicitly describes CO2-emissions forecasts.
CO2 is not identical to an all-greenhouse-gas CO2e inventory unless additional gases are included by method.
Aviation forecast scope must therefore be preserved when comparing with GHG inventories.
Forecast CO2 and territorial GHG totals use different statistical products.
International aviation treatment can differ across accounting frameworks.
Passenger forecasts and emissions forecasts are distinct output variables.
Aircraft movements and emissions are not interchangeable measures.
Scenario emissions are model results rather than parcel measurements.
Airport boundaries are not cadastral parcel boundaries.
Any parcel claim requires separate measured or attributable activity evidence.

packages.title: DfT aviation airport-scope QA
facts: The DfT 2026 aviation forecast covers UK airports.
Data tables accompany the forecast publication.
Disaggregated data tables are also provided.
The publication is intended to inform aviation strategy and policy.
It is used in analysis of aviation decarbonisation and airport policy.
An airport forecast may aggregate many terminals, runways and land holdings.
Airport-level activity does not identify individual parcel activity.
Forecast horizon and scenario must be retained for every value.
Observed historic statistics and forecast values must remain distinct.
No parcel emissions value is produced without a parcel-specific allocation method.

packages.title: International aviation/shipping memo-versus-territorial QA
facts: DESNZ provisional 2025 GHG statistics include estimates for international aviation and shipping.
The main provisional publication is based on UK territorial greenhouse gas accounting.
International aviation and shipping can be presented as additional memorandum information.
Memorandum items must not be silently added to or removed from a territorial total.
Accounting treatment must be retained when comparing transport totals.
International transport estimates are not local-authority parcel observations.
Provisional international transport estimates are subject to revision.
Fuel and activity assumptions may differ from domestic transport treatment.
CO2e totals and underlying fuel/activity data must remain distinct.
Parcel allocation is unsupported without specific operator and location evidence.

packages.title: International aviation/shipping provisional-method QA
facts: DESNZ published a methodology summary with the 2025 provisional GHG release.
The methodology distinguishes energy-use emissions derived from current energy data.
Some provisional components are held constant where updated data are not yet available.
Some non-energy emissions are derived from projections.
International aviation and shipping have a dedicated provisional methodology section.
Provisional estimates provide an early indication rather than final inventory values.
Final estimates may revise provisional values.
Method category must be retained alongside every provisional value.
A national provisional method is not a parcel measurement method.
Parcel values must remain absent where parcel-specific inputs are unavailable.

packages.title: DfT maritime model assumptions QA
facts: DfT published a maritime emissions modelling framework in March 2025.
The framework describes a model that estimates greenhouse gas emissions from shipping.
The model was developed to support analysis of the maritime decarbonisation strategy.
The framework documents assumptions and limitations.
Modelled shipping emissions are not direct measurements from every vessel.
Model results depend on the input and assumption set.
Shipping activity boundaries differ from land-parcel boundaries.
Strategy analysis and inventory accounting are distinct uses.
Model uncertainty must be preserved when using model outputs.
No port or parcel emissions value should be inferred without an explicit allocation method.

packages.title: Maritime strategy target-versus-observation QA
facts: The UK maritime decarbonisation strategy sets a long-term domestic maritime decarbonisation goal.
The strategy describes an aim for zero fuel-lifecycle GHG emissions by 2050.
It describes an interim reduction ambition for 2030 relative to 2008.
It describes a further interim reduction ambition for 2040 relative to 2008.
Targets are policy objectives rather than observed emissions.
Fuel-lifecycle GHG scope is not automatically identical to territorial inventory scope.
Target years must not be presented as measured outcomes.
Strategy targets do not identify emissions from an individual port parcel.
Modelled pathways must remain distinct from historic observations.
Parcel claims require actual parcel-linked activity or measured evidence.

packages.title: EA landfill methane method-comparability QA
facts: The Environment Agency published Landfill methane: measurement and metrics on 2 February 2026.
The project assessed methods for measuring methane emissions from landfills.
It considered how measurements could be used in regulation.
The project investigated two different measurement methods.
Different measurement methods should not be assumed interchangeable without method comparison.
Measured methane is distinct from modelled methane.
Measurement conditions and site operating state affect interpretation.
A landfill site boundary may contain multiple land parcels.
Site measurements are not automatically parcel measurements.
Any parcel attribution requires geometry and measurement-footprint evidence.

packages.title: EA landfill methane capture-effectiveness QA
facts: The Environment Agency project examined methane-emission measurement in relation to landfill gas management.
The project found measurement could potentially help improve landfill gas capture.
Reduced measured emissions can be relevant to assessing gas-management effectiveness.
Measurement of emitted methane is distinct from the amount of methane generated in waste.
Gas captured for treatment is distinct from residual methane emitted.
Operational conditions must be retained when comparing measurements.
A regulatory measurement concept does not create a national emissions inventory by itself.
Site-level methane evidence remains method-specific.
Landfill-site evidence must not be generalized to unrelated parcels.
Parcel attribution requires explicit spatial binding.

packages.title: EA landfill regulatory-use guard QA
facts: The 2026 Environment Agency project considered how methane measurements could be used in regulation.
The publication is research and assessment, not a universal requirement that every landfill use one measurement method.
Potential regulatory use must be distinguished from current permit conditions.
Measurement uncertainty must not be hidden when using results.
Research findings are not a direct substitute for reported Pollution Inventory values.
Landfill methane measurement and waste tonnage are different quantities.
Landfill methane measurement and captured-gas volume are different quantities.
A facility-level result is not automatically a parcel result.
Regulatory status and measurement status must both be preserved.
No parcel value is produced without site-to-parcel evidence.

packages.title: Ofgem DRHI Scheme Year 12 QA
facts: Ofgem published the Domestic RHI annual report for April 2025 to March 2026 on 17 July 2026.
The report covers Scheme Year 12.
The covered period is 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
The Domestic RHI promoted low-carbon heating technologies.
Eligible technologies included air-source heat pumps.
Eligible technologies included ground-source heat pumps.
Eligible technologies included biomass boilers.
Eligible technologies included solar thermal systems.
Scheme-year activity is an administrative programme measure.
Scheme activity is not a direct parcel greenhouse gas measurement.

packages.title: Ofgem DRHI expected-heat guard QA
facts: Domestic RHI payments were designed around eligible low-carbon heat installations.
Ofgem states eligible households could receive quarterly payments over seven years.
The scheme description refers to low-carbon heat the systems were expected to produce.
Expected heat is not automatically identical to metered heat for every installation.
Expected heat is not itself a measured greenhouse gas reduction.
Technology eligibility does not prove actual operating hours.
Scheme payment records do not identify cadastral parcel emissions without further linking.
Installations can remain in the payment lifecycle after the scheme closed to new applicants.
Administrative payments and physical heat output must remain distinct.
Parcel emissions require compatible activity and emissions-factor evidence.

packages.title: Ofgem DRHI closure-date QA
facts: Ofgem states the Domestic RHI closed to new applicants on 31 March 2022.
The 2025 to 2026 annual report therefore covers ongoing scheme activity after closure to new applicants.
Closure to new applicants does not mean all scheme payments stopped immediately.
Historic installations can remain relevant during their support period.
Application date, accreditation date and payment period are distinct fields.
Scheme closure date must be retained when interpreting new-installation counts.
Scheme activity is not equivalent to current national heat-pump deployment from all policies.
Administrative scheme boundaries must be preserved in comparisons.
Scheme records do not directly measure parcel GHG emissions.
Parcel inference remains forbidden without explicit parcel-linked evidence.

packages.title: Ofgem NDRHI Q1-2026 period QA
facts: Ofgem published Non-Domestic RHI Quarterly Report Issue 57 on 29 April 2026.
The report covers 1 January to 31 March 2026.
The Non-Domestic RHI supports renewable and low-carbon heat.
The quarterly report is an administrative scheme update.
The publication period must not be confused with its publication date.
Approved installations and generated heat are different metrics.
Technology mix and country mix are separate dimensions.
Quarterly scheme data do not represent every UK renewable-heat installation.
Scheme records are not parcel greenhouse gas measurements.
Parcel-level use requires installation-to-parcel and activity evidence.

packages.title: Ofgem NDRHI installation/heat/payment separation QA
facts: Ofgem NDRHI public reporting covers application and approved-installation counts.
It reports different renewable-heating technology types.
It reports approved installations by country.
It reports heat generated by approved installations.
It reports payments based on heat generated.
Installation count, capacity, heat output and payment value are distinct measures.
Biomethane treatment differs from direct heat-generating technologies in scheme reporting.
Country-level scheme totals are not parcel measurements.
Payment value is not a greenhouse gas emissions quantity.
Parcel emissions require physical activity and a compatible emissions method.

packages.title: Defra livestock-2025 activity-versus-emissions QA
facts: Defra's June 2025 livestock release covers commercial agricultural holdings in England.
The release reports cattle and calf populations.
It reports pig populations.
It reports sheep and lamb populations.
It reports poultry populations.
Livestock counts are agricultural activity data rather than direct GHG measurements.
Population change does not translate one-to-one into emissions change without an emissions model.
Species and production class matter to emissions modelling.
England totals do not identify the animals on a specific parcel.
Parcel emissions require holding or parcel linkage plus an appropriate emissions method.

packages.title: Defra livestock survey-method change QA
facts: Defra updated the June 2025 livestock release in March 2026.
The release states that some livestock information collection was simplified.
Some 'other livestock' data were no longer collected through the June Survey in the same way.
Method changes can affect comparability across years.
Headline livestock categories retain their own published series.
Survey estimates and administrative livestock-tracing data can have different provenance.
Method changes must be retained when evaluating trends.
A survey estimate is not a direct parcel census unless explicitly linked.
Livestock counts remain activity inputs rather than direct emissions measurements.
Parcel values must not be inferred from national average livestock densities.

packages.title: NAEI agriculture source-scope QA
facts: NAEI agriculture summaries identify enteric fermentation as a methane source.
They identify animal wastes and manure management as sources of methane and nitrous oxide.
They identify agricultural soils as an important nitrous-oxide source category.
They include fertiliser application among agricultural-soil emission drivers.
They include animal manures among agricultural-soil emission drivers.
They include crop residues and nitrogen processes among model inputs.
June Survey agricultural data are important activity inputs to agricultural inventory estimates.
Activity data are converted to emissions through inventory methods rather than treated as emissions directly.
National inventory source categories do not define cadastral parcels.
Parcel estimates require parcel-specific activity and a compatible inventory method.

packages.title: NAEI agriculture activity-to-model QA
facts: NAEI inventory estimates use agricultural activity datasets as model inputs.
Livestock numbers are not themselves tonnes of CO2e.
Fertiliser quantities are not themselves tonnes of CO2e.
Manure-management practices affect methane and nitrous-oxide estimates.
Emission factors and process assumptions are needed to convert activity to emissions.
Model outputs carry uncertainty from both activity data and methods.
Country or national assumptions cannot automatically represent one farm.
Holding-level activity does not automatically establish cadastral parcel geometry.
Inventory source-category totals must retain gas-species and method provenance.
No parcel GHG value should be fabricated when parcel activity is absent.

packages.title: Defra waste-2024/25 treatment-route QA
facts: Defra reported 25.2 million tonnes of local-authority managed waste in England in 2024/25.
Defra reported 1.4 million tonnes disposed via landfill in 2024/25.
Landfill represented 5.5% of local-authority waste in that period.
Defra reported 12.7 million tonnes sent for incineration in 2024/25.
Incineration represented 50.3% of local-authority waste in that period.
Defra reported 10.4 million tonnes sent for recycling in 2024/25.
Waste tonnage and greenhouse gas emissions are different quantities.
Treatment route strongly affects the emissions method that would be applicable.
Local-authority waste statistics do not identify emissions at an individual parcel.
Parcel emissions require site-specific treatment and emissions evidence.

packages.title: Defra IBA-metal recycling-rate QA
facts: Defra reported an England waste-from-households recycling rate of 43.8% for 2024.
Incinerator bottom ash metal is included in the published waste-from-households recycling rate.
Defra reported that IBA metal added about 1.0 percentage point to the 2024 rate.
When IBA metal is excluded, Defra reported a 42.8% recycling rate for 2024.
IBA-metal treatment changes the recycling-rate calculation.
A recycling rate is not a greenhouse gas emissions rate.
Waste classification rules must be preserved across comparisons.
Recycling-rate methodology can affect apparent trends without changing physical emissions directly.
Local-authority statistics are not cadastral parcel measurements.
Parcel emissions require treatment-facility and process-specific evidence.

packages.title: Defra local-authority waste-variation QA
facts: Defra reported substantial variation in household recycling rates across English local authorities in 2024/25.
The reported range was 17.0% to 63.9%.
Local-authority recycling performance is an area-level statistic.
Different local collection systems can affect reported recycling rates.
Area-level rates do not identify waste generated by a specific parcel.
Recycling rate is a proportion, not an emissions quantity.
Population and waste tonnage denominators must be kept distinct.
Financial-year and calendar-year waste measures must not be mixed silently.
Methodology and treatment-destination fields must be retained.
Parcel GHG estimates require parcel-specific waste activity and treatment data.

packages.title: Defra UK waste C&I coverage-lag QA
facts: UK Statistics on Waste includes commercial and industrial waste-generation statistics.
The data.gov summary notes UK C&I generation coverage through 2020.
It notes England C&I generation coverage through 2023.
Different waste topics in the release have different latest reference years.
Coverage lag must be retained when comparing waste categories.
UK and England geographic scopes must not be mixed.
Commercial and industrial waste tonnage is not direct greenhouse gas emissions.
Treatment route is required for many emissions calculations.
Aggregate C&I data do not identify individual sites or parcels.
Parcel attribution remains unsupported without site-specific records.

packages.title: DESNZ final GHG SIC-update timing QA
facts: DESNZ final UK GHG statistics provide territorial emissions estimates back to 1990.
Final estimates are first presented by source in the annual cycle.
DESNZ subsequently updates the publication to include end-user estimates.
DESNZ subsequently updates it to include Standard Industrial Classification estimates.
The data.gov final-GHG page was updated on 25 June 2026.
SIC estimates and source-sector estimates are different classification views.
Publication-cycle timing must be preserved when comparing editions.
Final status does not mean all future inventory revisions are impossible.
National SIC emissions are not parcel emissions.
Parcel attribution requires site-specific evidence and a defined allocation method.

packages.title: DESNZ final GHG territorial-boundary QA
facts: DESNZ final UK GHG statistics cover emissions occurring within the UK's borders.
This is a territorial accounting boundary.
Territorial accounting is distinct from ONS residence-basis Environmental Accounts.
Territorial accounting is also distinct from consumption-footprint accounting.
Comparisons must preserve the accounting basis.
National territorial emissions do not identify emitting parcels automatically.
Sector and SIC classifications are statistical groupings rather than cadastral geometries.
International aviation and shipping treatment must be checked separately.
Inventory revisions can update historical territorial estimates.
Parcel emissions remain unsupported without location-linked activity or measured emissions data.
